Physics.q: A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of 360 km/h at an altitude of 2 km, drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point O, 20 s after it is dropped. Displacement of 'O' from the position of helicopter where the object was released is: (use g = 10 m/s²)
Physics.hint: Calculate horizontal and vertical displacements separately, then find the resultant vector.

Physics.q: For a train engine moving with speed of 20 m/s, the driver must apply brakes at a distance of 500 m before the station for the train to come to rest at the station. If the brakes were applied at half of this distance, the train engine would cross the station with speed √x m/s. The value of x is:
Physics.hint: Use the third equation of motion: v² = u² + 2as.

Physics.q: The maximum error in the measurement of resistance, current and time for which current flows in an electrical circuit are 1%, 2% and 3% respectively. The maximum percentage error in the detection of the dissipated heat will be:
Physics.hint: Heat H = I²Rt. Apply error analysis formula: ΔH/H = 2(ΔI/I) + ΔR/R + Δt/t.

Chemistry.q: Mass of magnesium required to produce 220 mL of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dil. HCl is:
Chemistry.hint: 1 mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L at STP. Calculate moles of H₂ first.

Chemistry.q: 10 mL of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion gives 40 mL of CO₂(g) and 50 mL of water vapour. Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is:
Chemistry.hint: Apply the general combustion equation: CxHy + (x + y/4)O₂ → xCO₂ + (y/2)H₂O.

Chemistry.q: The number of radial node(s) for 3p orbital is:

Mathematics.q: The number of solutions of the equation e^(sin x) - 2e^(-sin x) = 2 is:
Mathematics.hint: Substitute e^(sin x) = t and solve the quadratic equation. Check the domain of sin x.

Mathematics.q: The total number of two digit numbers 'n', such that 3^n + 7^n is a multiple of 10, is:
Mathematics.hint: Analyze the unit digits of powers of 3 and 7 for odd and even values of n.

Mathematics.q: The number of real roots of the equation √(x² - 4x + 3) + √(x² - 9) = √(4x² - 14x + 6) is:
Mathematics.hint: Factorize the expressions inside the square roots and determine the valid domain for x.

Mathematics.q: The remainder on dividing 5^99 by 11 is:
Mathematics.hint: Use Fermat's Little Theorem or binomial expansion.

Physics.q: Train A and train B are running on parallel tracks in the opposite directions with speed of 36 km/h and 72 km/h, respectively. A person is walking in train A in the direction opposite to its motion with a speed of 1.8 km/h. Speed (in m/s) of this person as observed from train B will be close to:
Physics.hint: Convert all speeds to m/s and use relative velocity concepts.

Physics.q: A steel block of 10 kg rests on a horizontal floor. When three iron cylinders of 20 kg each are placed on it, the block and cylinders go down with an acceleration 0.2 m/s². The normal reaction R' by the floor is (in N): [Take g = 10 m/s²]
Physics.hint: Draw the free body diagram for the entire system and apply Newton's Second Law.

Physics.q: A river is flowing from west to east direction with speed of 9 km/h. If a boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of 27 km/h in still water, crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of 150° to direction of river flow, then the width of the river is:
Physics.hint: Find the component of the boat's velocity perpendicular to the river flow.

Chemistry.q: An ideal gas (Cv = 5/2 R) is expanded adiabatically against a constant pressure of 1 atm until it doubles in volume. If the initial temperature and pressure is 298 K and 5 atm, respectively then the final temperature is (nearest integer):
Chemistry.hint: For an irreversible adiabatic expansion, W = ΔU. Use -P_ext(V2 - V1) = nCv(T2 - T1).

Chemistry.q: The equilibrium constant Kc at 298 K for the reaction A + B ⇌ C + D is 100. Starting with an equimolar solution with concentrations of A, B, C and D all equal to 1M, the equilibrium concentration of D is (x × 10^-2) M. The value of x is:
Chemistry.hint: Set up an ICE table starting from 1M each and equate to Kc.

Chemistry.q: When 1 g each of compounds AB and AB₂ are dissolved in 15 g of water separately, they increased the boiling point of water by 2.7 K and 1.5 K respectively. The atomic mass of A (in amu) is x/10. The value of x is: (Kb = 0.5 K kg/mol)
Chemistry.hint: Use ΔTb = Kb × m to find the molar masses of AB and AB₂.

Mathematics.q: If α and β are the distinct roots of the equation x² + (3)^(1/4)x + 3^(1/2) = 0 then the value of α^96(α^12 - 1) + β^96(β^12 - 1) is equal to:
Mathematics.hint: Transform the equation into a form where roots can be expressed using cube roots of unity (ω).

Mathematics.q: Let P = {z ∈ C : |z + 2 - 3i| ≤ 1} and Q = {z ∈ C : z(1 + i) + z*(1 - i) ≤ -8}. Let in P ∩ Q, |z - 3 + 2i| be maximum and minimum at z₁ and z₂ respectively. If |z₁|² + 2|z₂|² = α + β√2, then α + β equals:
Mathematics.hint: Identify the geometrical shapes (circle and half-plane) and find the extreme points on the intersection.

Mathematics.q: In an examination, there are 5 multiple choice questions with 3 choices, out of which exactly one is correct. There are 3 marks for each correct answer, -2 marks for each wrong answer. Then, the number of ways a student gets 5 marks is:
Mathematics.hint: Determine the number of correct, incorrect, and unattempted questions needed to sum up to exactly 5 marks.

Mathematics.q: If the sum of the second, fourth and sixth terms of a G.P. of positive terms is 21 and the sum of its eighth, tenth and twelfth terms is 15309, then the sum of its first nine terms is:
Mathematics.hint: Set up equations for the sums and divide them to find the common ratio 'r'.

Physics.q: A body of mass 0.5 kg travels on straight line path with velocity v = (3x² + 4) m/s. The net work done by the force during its displacement from x = 0 to x = 2 m is:
Physics.hint: Calculate initial and final velocities, then apply the Work-Energy Theorem.

Physics.q: A satellite of 10³ kg mass is revolving in circular orbit of radius 2R. If 10⁴R/6 J energy is supplied to the satellite, it would revolve in a new circular orbit of radius: (use g = 10 m/s²)
Physics.hint: Total energy in orbit is -GMm/2r. Add the supplied energy to find the new total energy.

Physics.q: A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
Physics.hint: Apply Archimedes' principle. Mass of water displaced equals the mass of the cube.

Physics.q: Two simple harmonic motions are represented by the equations y₁ = 10 sin(3πt + π/3) and y₂ = 5(sin 3πt + √3 cos 3πt). Ratio of amplitude of y₁ to y₂ = x : 1. The value of x is:
Physics.hint: Convert y₂ into a standard sine function using trigonometric identities to find its amplitude.

Chemistry.q: A 2.0 g sample containing MnO₂ is treated with HCl liberating Cl₂. The Cl₂ gas is passed into a solution of KI and 60.0 mL of 0.1 M Na₂S₂O₃ is required to titrate the liberated iodine. The percentage of MnO₂ in the sample is: (nearest integer)
Chemistry.hint: Use the concept of milliequivalents. Equivalents of MnO₂ = Equivalents of Cl₂ = Equivalents of I₂ = Equivalents of Na₂S₂O₃.

Chemistry.q: The number of acidic oxides among VO₂, V₂O₃, CrO₃, V₂O₅ and Mn₂O₇ is X. The primary valency of cobalt in [Co(en)₃]₂(SO₄)₃ is Y. The value of X + Y is:
Chemistry.hint: Higher oxidation state oxides are generally more acidic. Primary valency relates to the oxidation state of the metal.

Chemistry.q: The number of optically active products obtained from the complete ozonolysis of 3,6-dimethyloct-4-ene is:
Chemistry.hint: Analyze the products of ozonolysis for chiral centers and plane of symmetry.

Mathematics.q: For positive integers n, if 4a_n = (n² + 5n + 6) and S_n = Σ (1/a_k) from k=1 to n, then the value of 507 S_2025 is:
Mathematics.hint: Factorize the quadratic expression and use the method of partial fractions (telescoping series).

Mathematics.q: For n ≥ 2, let S_n denote the set of all subsets of {1, 2, ..., n} with no two consecutive numbers. Then n(S_5) is equal to:
Mathematics.hint: This follows the Fibonacci sequence pattern.

Mathematics.q: The product of the last two digits of (1919)^1919 is:
Mathematics.hint: Find (1919)^1919 mod 100. Write 1919 as (1900 + 19) or use binomial expansion on (20 - 1).

Physics.q: A physical quantity C is related to four other quantities as C = pq² / (r³ √s). The percentage errors in p, q, r, s are 1%, 2%, 3%, 2%. The percentage error in C will be:
Physics.hint: Error = Δp/p + 2(Δq/q) + 3(Δr/r) + 0.5(Δs/s).

Physics.q: A particle is moving with constant acceleration a. The v² versus x plot passes through (10, 40) and (20, 60). The acceleration of the particle is (in m/s²):
Physics.hint: Use v² = u² + 2as. The slope of v² vs x graph gives 2a.

Chemistry.q: 3 moles of an ideal gas at 300 K expand isothermally from 30 dm³ to 45 dm³ against a constant opposing pressure of 80 kPa. The amount of heat transferred is (in J):
Chemistry.hint: For isothermal process, Q = -W. W = -P_ext(V2 - V1).

Chemistry.q: x mg of Mg(OH)₂ (molar mass = 58) is required to be dissolved in 1.0 L of water to produce a pH of 10.0 at 298 K. The value of x is (Nearest integer):
Chemistry.hint: Find pOH, then [OH⁻]. [Mg²⁺] will be half of [OH⁻]. Calculate mass from moles.

Mathematics.q: Let A = {θ ∈ [0, 2π] : 1 + 10 Re( (2cosθ + isinθ)/(cosθ - 3isinθ) ) = 0}. Then Σ θ² is equal to:
Mathematics.hint: Rationalize the complex number by multiplying with conjugate of denominator to find real part.

Mathematics.q: Let the mean and standard deviation of 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 7, a, b be 4 and √2 respectively. The mean deviation about the mode of these observations is:
Mathematics.hint: First identify the mode (most frequent), then find a and b using mean and variance formulas.

Physics.q: A body of mass m is suspended by two strings making angles 30° and 60° with the horizontal ceiling with tensions T₁ and T₂. If T₁ = √3 T₂, the correct relation is:
Physics.hint: Balance forces horizontally and vertically. T₁ cosθ₁ = T₂ cosθ₂ and T₁ sinθ₁ + T₂ sinθ₂ = mg.

Physics.q: A rod of length 5L is bent at right angle keeping one side length as 2L and other 3L. If L=10cm, position of centre of mass of the system is:
Physics.hint: Find COM of individual segments and use X_cm = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂)/(m₁ + m₂).

Chemistry.q: Which of the following binary mixture does not show the behaviour of minimum boiling azeotropes?
Chemistry.hint: Phenol and aniline show negative deviation from Raoult's law (maximum boiling azeotrope).

Chemistry.q: 1.80 g of solute A was dissolved in 62.5 cm³ of ethanol (density 0.8 g/cm³) and freezing point was 155.1 K. If Tf of ethanol is 156.0 K and Kf is 2.00, molar mass of A is:
Chemistry.hint: Use ΔTf = Kf × m. Remember to calculate the mass of solvent using density and volume.

Mathematics.q: Let p be the number of triangles and q be the number of quadrilaterals formed by joining vertices of a regular polygon of n sides. If p+q = 126, eccentricity of x²/16 + y²/n = 1 is:
Mathematics.hint: p = nC3, q = nC4. Solve for n, then find eccentricity using e = √(1 - b²/a²).

Mathematics.q: Let matrix A³ = A + I (effectively A^n = A^(n-2) + A^2 - I for n≥3). The sum of all elements of A^50 for the given 3x3 matrix is:
Mathematics.hint: Find a pattern for A^n by substituting smaller values of n.

Physics.q: A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a solid sphere of mass 20 kg kept on a rough horizontal plane. If it rolls without slipping, acceleration of its center is (in m/s²):
Physics.hint: Use F + f = ma and torque equation F.R - f.R = Iα. Solve for a.

Physics.q: The variation of acceleration due to gravity (g) with distance (r) from the center of the earth is correctly represented by a graph which is:
Physics.hint: Inside Earth, g ∝ r. Outside Earth, g ∝ 1/r².

Chemistry.q: The quantity of silver deposited when one coulomb charge is passed through AgNO₃ solution is:
Chemistry.hint: Faraday's first law: m = ZQ. If Q = 1 C, m = Z (electrochemical equivalent).

Chemistry.q: Half life of zero order reaction A -> product is 1 hour for initial conc 2.0 M. Time required to decrease A from 0.50 M to 0.25 M is:
Chemistry.hint: For zero order, t_1/2 is directly proportional to initial concentration.

Mathematics.q: The system of equations x+5y-z=1, 4x+3y-3z=7, 24x+y+λz=μ has infinitely many solutions. If x, y, z are integers and 7 ≤ x+y+z ≤ 77, the number of solutions is:
Mathematics.hint: Apply condition for infinite solutions (Δ = 0, Δx = Δy = Δz = 0) to find relation between x, y, z.

Mathematics.q: The number of integral terms in the expansion of (5^(1/2) + 7^(1/8))^1016 is:
Mathematics.hint: General term involves 5^(r/2) and 7^((1016-r)/8). Both r/2 and (1016-r)/8 must be integers.

Physics.q: Under isothermal condition, the pressure of a gas is given by P = aV⁻³. The bulk modulus at constant temperature is equal to:
Physics.hint: Bulk Modulus B = -V(dP/dV). Differentiate P with respect to V.

Physics.q: The amount of work done to break a big water drop of radius R into 27 small drops of equal radius is 10 J. Work done required to break the same big drop into 64 small drops is (in J):
Physics.hint: Work done is proportional to change in surface area. W ∝ (n^(1/3) - 1).

Chemistry.q: The atomic number of the element with lowest 1st ionisation enthalpy among elements with atomic numbers 32, 35, 87, 19 is:
Chemistry.hint: Ionisation enthalpy decreases down a group. Look for the heaviest alkali metal.

Chemistry.q: Which of the following molecules show paramagnetic behavior? (A) O₂, (B) N₂, (C) F₂, (D) S₂, (E) Cl₂
Chemistry.hint: Use Molecular Orbital Theory. Check for unpaired electrons in anti-bonding orbitals.

Mathematics.q: A random variable X takes values 0,1,2,3 with P(X=0)=P(X=1)=p and P(X=2)=P(X=3)=q. If E(X²) = 2E(X), then the value of 8p - 1 is:
Mathematics.hint: Use definitions of Expected Value. Sum of all probabilities must be 1.

Mathematics.q: The number of solutions of the equation (4-√3)sinx - 2√3 cos²x = -4/(1+√3) in the interval [-2π, 5π/2] is:
Mathematics.hint: Convert cos²x to 1 - sin²x to form a quadratic in sin x. Solve for valid angles.

Physics.q: A light hollow cube of side 10 cm and mass 10g is floating in water. Pushed down and released, its time period of oscillation is yπ × 10⁻² s. Value of y is (g = 10 m/s², density = 1000 kg/m³):
Physics.hint: Time period T = 2π√(m/k), where restoring force constant k = ρ A g.

Physics.q: The internal energy of air in a 4m x 4m x 3m room at 1 atm is X × 10⁶ J. Value of X is (Consider air as diatomic):
Physics.hint: U = (f/2)PV. For diatomic gas f = 5. V = length × breadth × height.

Chemistry.q: Group 14 elements A and B have 1st IE 708 and 715 kJ/mol (lowest in group). The nature of their stable ions A²⁺ and B⁴⁺ respectively is:
Chemistry.hint: Elements are Sn and Pb. Due to inert pair effect, Pb²⁺ is more stable than Pb⁴⁺, and Sn⁴⁺ is more stable than Sn²⁺.

Chemistry.q: The number of colourless lanthanoid ions among Eu³⁺, Lu³⁺, Nd³⁺, La³⁺, Sm³⁺ is:
Chemistry.hint: Ions with f^0 or f^14 configuration are colourless due to absence of f-f transition.

Mathematics.q: The value of limit x->0 [ cosec x (√(2cos²x + 3cosx) - √(cos²x + sinx + 4)) ] is:
Mathematics.hint: Rationalize the numerator and use L'Hopital's rule or standard limits as x tends to 0.

Mathematics.q: If f(x) = (1+ax)^(1/x) for x<0, 1+b for x=0, and ((x+4)^(1/2)-2)/((x+6)^(1/3)-2) for x>0 is continuous at x=0. Then e^a b c (where c is the RHL) is:
Mathematics.hint: Equate Left Hand Limit, Right Hand Limit and f(0). Use standard limit formula for (1+x)^(1/x).
